headline: Interactive front ends wrap established omics, imaging and mutational scanning analyses
label: Interactive Omics Analysis Frameworks
summary: Recent preprints and papers offer deployable, code-light interfaces for spatial, proteomic, single-cell and MRI datasets that previously required scripting.
synthesis: The dominant thread is packaging established analyses in interactive or graphical front ends for users who may not program. Several items are code-free or near code-free: SMEW (Shiny, spatial metabolomics MSI), DIA-NN EasyFilter (KNIME workflow for PARQUET output) and CountESS (graphical pipeline for deep mutational scanning). Others provide code-accessible interfaces: MatriSpace (R package and Shiny app), OmicsMLMentor (web app offering 15 ML models) and NeuroStream (Streamlit tool for ComBat harmonization of multicohort MRI). DoTools instead addresses interoperability, wrapping scVI, CellTypist and CellBender across Seurat, SCE and Scanpy workflows in R and Python. What is new is the consolidation of steps such as filtering, harmonization, model ranking and visualization within single environments; the items do not claim methodological novelty in the underlying analyses.
